title: Capacity Commitment Intake: staged approvals, throughput SLAs, and planning cadence
creator: Rhea Kapoor
description: Build a formal intake and staged-approval workflow for Dedicated capacity commitments that ties customer reservation requests to verifiable throughput SLAs, autoscaling templates, and a maintainable capacity ledger. This ticket covers the intake schema, the three approval gates (technical, commercial, security), standard throughput SLA tiers with burst rules, autoscale policy templates per tier, and the planning cadence to sync committed capacity with forecasting and fleet controls.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype captures required fields: customer, contact, region(s), model family, expected steady qps and peak qps, average token length, preferred SLA tier, desired start/end dates, contract duration, and billing PO/reference.
Define and publish 3 throughput SLA tiers (Tier A/B/C) with clear baseline throughput, burst windows, and measurable SLOs (p95 latency, sustained QPS).
Approval gates implemented: technical validation checklist (ENG), commercial terms check (Sales/PM), and security/compliance sign-off. Each gate produces an auditable decision in the Console.
Autoscaling policy templates created and codified for each SLA tier (min/max capacity, scale latency, cooldowns, burst buffers) and validated with a simulation harness.
Capacity ledger prototype that records commitments, actual usage, decommit windows, and ownership; integrates with forecasting (weekly cadence) and shows predicted vs committed capacity.
Console UX mocks for submit/approve/reject flow and an initial API to create/modify reservation requests.
End-to-end test plan and one pilot onboarding with an internal team to validate process and metrics collection.
progress_updates: 2025-01-22: Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting with ENG, Security, and Sales. Agreed on three-tier SLA model as starting point.
2025-01-29: Draft intake form fields circulated; Elena Torres (ENG) flagged need for KV cache/sequence-length capture to size capacity accurately.
2025-02-02: Autoscale policy templates sketched; simulation harness scoped under ENG-7021. Marcus to own coordination with Forecasting team.
2025-02-06: Design (Zara Noor) provided first Console flow; Security (Priya Singh) requested mandatory encryption/KMS field for private deployments.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use tiered SLA (A/B/C) instead of fully custom SLAs to reduce approval friction and speed onboarding.
Trade-off: Fixed tiers may be suboptimal for very large enterprise commits; we will add 'custom SLA' pathway requiring senior approver.
Decision: Autoscale templates will default to conservative cooldowns for Tier A (low latency) to avoid oscillation; higher tiers get more aggressive scaling for cost efficiency.
Trade-off: Conservative cooldowns increase short-term cost under bursty workloads but protect p95 latency. We'll monitor pilot and adjust.
review_feedback: Elena Torres (ENG): Need explicit technical validation steps for persistent KV cache sizing and model quantization constraints. Recommended adding a pre-flight load test for >=75% of requested throughput.
Priya Singh (Security): Require a security checklist as a gating item for private/VPC deployments (KMS config, audit log retention, data residency).
Ben Carter (Sales): Asked for a simplified one-page summary of SLA terms and expected billing cadence to share with customers.
Zara Noor (Design): Requested a secondary UX path for simple renewals and amendment flow to reduce friction for existing customers.
open_questions: What is the exact decommitment window (notice period) for early contract termination without penalty? (Legal/Finance input required)
How granular should the capacity ledger be: per-customer, per-team, or per-reservation instance?
Should we expose an internal 'soft-reserve' status for trials that locks headroom but is not a contractual commit?
How will we verify customer-provided traffic profiles vs actual patterns to reconcile billing/penalties?
